I'll carefully compare the source text against the draft, hunting for signature losses.

**Key observations:**

1. The famous "democratic God" passage concludes the source with "Thou who, in all Thy mighty, earthly marchings, ever cullest Thy selectest champions from the kingly commons; bear me out in it, O God!" — The draft cuts the final two clauses after "higher than a throne!" — dropping the culminating rhetorical climax.

2. The "most sorrowful, nay shocking, to expose the fall of valour" passage and the setup before the democratic dignity paragraph — the source has "scarce might I have the heart to write it; for it is a thing most sorrowful, nay shocking, to expose the fall of valour in the soul. Men may seem detestable as joint stock-companies and nations..." The draft jumps directly to "man, in the ideal, is so noble..." cutting the transition and the "joint stock-companies" passage which is distinctive stylistically and critically noted.

3. The "rainbow over his disastrous set of sun" clause and "if I shall touch that workman's arm with some ethereal light; if I shall spread a rainbow over his disastrous set of sun" — these lines are cut from the "If, then, to meanest mariners" paragraph in the draft.

4. The Starbuck physical description — "like a revivified Egyptian" and "like a patent chronometer" comparisons — are absent. These are distinctively Melvillean images.

5. The closing line of the entire chapter: "bear me out in it, O God!" — cut.
